issues.legal_issue: A family partition that adjusts existing rights without transferring property is not a disposition qualifying property for the estate-duty exemption for a life interest that reverts to the disponer.
material_facts: A widow gave up rights to inherit part of the family property and to receive maintenance in exchange for an allotment of land for her lifetime.
The widow could not alienate the land, and her interest ended on her death, after which the land passed to members of the former family.
The allotment was made under a registered partition deed and formed part of an adjustment of the family members’ rights.
issues.conclusion: The partition was an adjustment of rights, not a disposition, so the exemption under section 24 did not apply. The interest ceasing on the widow’s death fell within section 7, and the land was not exempt from estate duty.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 7(1) of the Estate Duty Act, 1953, property in which an interest ceases on the deceased’s death is deemed to pass to the extent a benefit accrues from that cessation. Section 24(1) provides an exception for property where a disposition confers a life or death-determinable interest on a person and the remainder is conferred absolutely on the disponer. A Hindu family partition is an adjustment of existing rights, not a transfer or disposition: Commissioner of Income-tax, Gujarat v. Keshavlal Lallubhai Patel, which approved Gutta Radhakrishnayya v. Gutta Sarasamma, and Commissioner of Gift Tax, Madras v. M.S. Getti Chettiar. The Court applied the same contextual meaning of “disposition” to section 24.

rule.if: estate_duty_dispute and family_partition_adjusted_existing_rights and life_interest_ended_at_death and property_passed_to_former_family_members

predicates.estate_duty_dispute: The proceeding concerns whether property is liable to estate duty.
predicates.family_partition_adjusted_existing_right: Family members partitioned family property by adjusting rights they already held, and an allotment was made to a family member in exchange for relinquished rights.
predicates.life_interest_ended_at_death: The recipient’s interest in the allotted property was limited to the recipient’s lifetime and ended on the recipient’s death.
predicates.property_passed_to_former_family_members: On the recipient’s death, the property passed to members of the former family.

issues.definition: When an estate-duty dispute concerns property allotted in a family partition that adjusted existing rights, and the recipient’s lifetime interest ended with the property passing to former family members, the property is not exempt from estate duty.
